mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES has risen monotonically for three consecutive weeks (4.7, 5.1, 5.6, 7.1) and a continuation of this commuting recovery adds weekday footfall to retail districts, so the mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days will exceed its last-28-day mean of 0.5.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose 4.7 to 7.1 across t-3w to t-0w
regime_hint: reopening with gradual return to workplaces
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to 0.5 while WORKPLACES holds above 7.0 for at least two of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has recovered from 0.9 to 2.1 and a sustained move above the +2.0 level marks restored transit-based shopping trips; once TRANSIT holds above 2.0 for two consecutive weeks, RETAIL_REC rises over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean at or above 2.0 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved 0.9 to 2.1 over t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT holds at or above 2.0 for two consecutive weeks but the following two-week mean of RETAIL_REC is below the preceding two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES rises while RESIDENTIAL simultaneously falls, out-of-home time is being reallocated from the home to commercial districts; the joint signal, not either series alone, predicts higher discretionary retail footfall over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below 3.6 in the same week WORKPLACES weekly mean rises above 6.0
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL eased 3.7 to 3.4 while WORKPLACES rose 5.6 to 7.1 in the latest week
regime_hint: reopening with partial return to office and reduced residential time
failure_condition: In weeks where RESIDENTIAL falls below 3.6 and WORKPLACES rises above 6.0, the following two-week RETAIL_REC mean is flat or lower.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has held between 42.6 and 49.3 for four straight weeks, a roughly 48-point elevation signalling persistent household stock-up and trip consolidation; sustained high grocery activity absorbs shopping trips that would otherwise reach retail-and-recreation venues, so RETAIL_REC drifts lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean stays above 45 for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed in the 42.6-49.3 band across all four snapshot weeks
regime_hint: elevated precautionary shopping and stock-up regime
failure_condition: The next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds its last-28-day mean of 0.5 while GROCERY_PHARM remains above 45 for the whole period.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS jumped 5.0 points in the latest week (-7.6 to -2.6), the largest single-week gain across all categories; outdoor leisure activity co-moves with recreation spending, so RETAIL_REC rises within one week of a PARKS improvement exceeding 4 points.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean improves by more than 4.0 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -7.6 to -2.6 between t-1w and t-0w
regime_hint: winter holiday period with mild outdoor conditions
failure_condition: In the week following a PARKS improvement larger than 4 points, the weekly RETAIL_REC mean declines relative to the trigger week.

mechanism_narrative: With WORKPLACES rising and RESIDENTIAL flat-to-down (3.9 to 3.4), the snapshot shows no sign of reinstated stay-at-home orders; absent new restrictions through the holiday peak, retail-and-recreation mobility continues its climb over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:no category shows a restriction-style collapse; WORKPLACES above baseline and RESIDENTIAL below 4.0 in every week
regime_hint: holiday peak with no reinstated stay-at-home mandates
failure_condition: The next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC falls below 0.5 even though WORKPLACES stays above baseline and RESIDENTIAL stays below 4.0 throughout.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS remains below baseline (-2.6) while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated at 3.4, a cold-weather home-centric pattern in which discretionary trips are curtailed; so long as PARKS does not cross above zero, the weekly RETAIL_REC mean stays at or below its current level.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS never rose above -2.6 and RESIDENTIAL never fell below 3.4 in the snapshot
regime_hint: winter cold-weather home-centric regime with suppressed outdoor activity
failure_condition: While PARKS stays below 0.0, the weekly RETAIL_REC mean rises above 1.1 in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM decelerating from 49.3 to 48.3 while WORKPLACES accelerates from 5.6 to 7.1 indicates trip reallocation away from grocery stock-up toward other destinations; this joint signal predicts a higher RETAIL_REC mean over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls week-on-week while WORKPLACES rises week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM eased 49.3 to 48.3 while WORKPLACES rose 5.6 to 7.1 in the latest week
regime_hint: post-stock-up normalization with reallocated shopping trips
failure_condition: When GROCERY_PHARM falls week-on-week and WORKPLACES rises week-on-week, the following two-week mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below the preceding two-week mean.
